label: F-4f95e8

findings.note: Plan D3 explicitly specifies `string QuotaKeyOf(string model) => string.Empty`, and ReviewerRuntime.cs and QuotaCooldowns.cs:116-124 implement exactly that string-keyed contract, so this asks for something the plan decided against.

Plan D5 puts the per-key grouping, the spent-wins-over-Ok choice and the `Spent ?? Hopeless` qualification in AfterRoundAsync, and puts the vendor reset in the runtime's ReadResetAsync; QuotaCooldowns.cs:181-203 and AntigravityRuntime.cs:47-70 do exactly this, and the 'future verdict bypassed' failure is speculative.

The decision is made outside the lock (QuotaCooldowns.cs:140-147), and ParkChange.AppliedTo (:370-379) does not re-check under the lock, so a later round's lift can be overwritten by an older park; but the plan deliberately runs the probe outside the lock, and the scenario needs a spent refusal followed by a real success on the same quota within one probe window, which is rare and bounded by expiry.

AfterRoundAsync awaits each key's probe one after another (QuotaCooldowns.cs:140-143), and each probe is bounded at 30 s (AgyQuotaReport.cs:214), so three spent agy groups can delay the summary by about 90 s; this is real but a worst case, because unknown groups are not probed (AntigravityRuntime.cs:57-59) and a normal /quota answer is fast.

Plan D6 and S15 specify that a non-parseable answer is CannotCheck("no report in the answer"), which AgyQuotaReport.cs:108-121 and :239-241 implement; a more detailed diagnostic is a matter of taste, and both cases give the same fail-safe result.

Plan D5 defines ReadResetAsync with an IProcessLauncher parameter, called from AfterRoundAsync; passing the launcher through (QuotaCooldowns.cs:131-134) is the direct way to do that, and swapping it for a delegate is a matter of taste.

Plan D3 explicitly decides on 'one explicit, measured table', says an unknown family gets its own `antigravity/?<model>` key, and says adding a family is one table row; AgyQuotaReport.cs:33-55 and its remarks at :15 already document this contract.

The rambling claim describes plan-mandated behaviour: plan D3 says an unknown agy model has 'no gauge-based parking' and that a Spent==true refusal still parks on stated/guess, which AntigravityRuntime.cs:57-68 does without probing, and the bucket lookup for known keys works.

The data folder is created first by FolderRefusal (QuotaCooldowns.cs:301-313); HeldFile.TakenByDotNet catches UnauthorizedAccess, DirectoryNotFound, PathTooLong and IOException and returns them as Unusable or Busy (HeldFile.cs); and AfterRoundAsync has a catch-all (QuotaCooldowns.cs:150-153), so nothing escapes to the engine.

WithVendorSentence (QuotaCooldowns.cs:232-233) already passes the reason through VendorReason.Written, which is Redaction.SafeText(reason, SafetyCap) (VendorReason.cs:31), so the reason is already capped before it is joined; this is not a security issue.
Plan D4 says 'read on every CanRun, no cache (it is under 16 KiB for ever)', on purpose, so that other processes' parks are seen; PanelService.CoolingOf documents and implements that decision.

This side's notes store an absolute ISO instant, not a relative duration (AntigravityRuntime.cs:62); the live '(in N h)' is computed at read time in CooldownSentences.When, and in cooldownWords at render; the only stale duration is the vendor's quoted sentence, which plan D4 and D9 require in the note and tooltip.
AgyError.Parse (AgyError.cs:42-75) runs once per failed agy launch over stderr that has already been redacted; span-level micro-optimisation there gives no practical gain.

missed: Under the lock, ParkChange.AppliedTo (QuotaCooldowns.cs:370-379) overwrites an entry that another process wrote after this round's decision, without comparing any ordering; this is the same root cause as R1-2, but it also lets a shorter park replace a longer one that stands.
AfterRoundAsync calls the synchronous Mutate (QuotaCooldowns.cs:147), and HeldFile.TakeWithin can block a thread-pool thread for up to the 30 s lock wait inside an async round path.
summary: Of 13 findings, only two (the stale-park race and the sequential probes) point at real but minor behaviour; most of the rest ask for things the plan explicitly decided against (string keys, the explicit table, no cache, the fixed CannotCheck text) or misread the code (exception handling, note truncation, unknown-group handling). A team that acted on this review would gain little, and several 'Major' labels are clearly inflated.
